Old Nav vs New Nav

The old nav computer mapped the same way the walk sheet maps the new one, then the two put side by side: every screen, every control, what the new menus lost, what they gained, the two things you named, and a numbered list of what to change. You answer the list by number.

Old-nav screenshots captured live 2026-09-18 on lane A in Sol at your window (2021×1162, so the old canvas is 1981×1122). New-design screenshots are the walk sheet's, still current: no code under src/ has changed since. Behaviour rows come from a code read of every handler by 21 readers, three cross-checks and a critic; the two figures marked measured were driven live.

How to read this

Three looks: LEGACY is the old nav (press V from design 2 to get it). DESIGN 1 is the rail. DESIGN 2 is bars. The tags in the comparison tables say what happened to each function on the way from old to new.

SAME same input, same result CHANGED reachable, but by a different input or with a different result LOST the old nav did it, no new path exists NEW no old equivalent RULED a difference you decided on record DEAD coded, cannot fire HIDDEN works, advertised nowhere
Nothing here is a judgment of how the screens look. Where a table says "lost" it means a control or a readout has no path in the new design; whether it should come back is yours, in the list at the bottom.

After the fixes — what to look at

Items 1–12 and the review's ten defects are built, tested and live-checked (workstream nav-defects-batch-2026-09-18, lane A). These captures are the parts a script cannot judge; the rest was measured. Captured live in Sol at your window after the batch.

Two of these are decisions dressed as fixes: the ladder no longer follows the sort key (it keeps AU order so its letters can match the rail), and design 1's tab strip lost its level count to make room for the legend (the same number still prints at the top of the rail). Say so if either is wrong.

What the new menus lost, and what they gained

Ranked by how much the pilot forfeits. Items you already ruled on are marked. "Both" means neither design has it.

#LostWhere the old nav had itCost to the pilot
1Hover-inspect on every screensector name (GALAXY), coordinates (SECTOR, REGION), star tooltip (PRISM), body callout (SYSTEM)Nothing on the map identifies itself before a click. In design 1 the rail carries the facts after a click; in design 2 the map itself carries almost none.
2Planet detail with moonsSYSTEM: click a planet with moonsMoons cannot be seen on their orbits or chosen as burn targets; a pip click selects the parent.
3The prism's depth cuesdrop lines to the plane, the plane grid, far-first drawing, halo, multiplicity glyphHeight above the plane is the prism's whole point and now reads only from a mark's vertical position on a coarser grid.
4Names on the prism and the orreryevery catalogue star; every bodyDesign 1's prism shows eight digits and no names; both SYSTEM pictures show ordinal tags. The name is one click away in a list, not on the thing.
5Height numbers and the real minimapHEIGHT with disk region, PLAYER Y, Y RANGE, minimap with camera and view rectangleNo number says how far above the plane you are in either design; design 2's corner widget shows a scale mark only.
6Wheel zoom at SYSTEMorrery scales 0.3× to 5×The wheel still changes a value; nothing draws it.
7Ship position and trajectorySHIP diamond at the real body, dashed line to the targetYou cannot see where you are in the system or where a burn would take you.
8Wide-binary companionsfar-companion chips and the component viewDesign 2 prints the separation; the member list and the sub-orrery are gone in both.
9Two of the four ways to closethe × and the backdropUnder the designs the × is off-screen and the backdrop is covered; N and Esc remain.
10Belt names, star facts, off-map target arrowASTEROID / KUIPER BELT; class, radius, age, planet count; the edge arrowBelts are anonymous dots, the star has no line of text, a target outside the 2D frame gives no bearing.
11AUTOPILOT togglebottom-left buttonWithdrawn under both designs. It is inert in ORRERY anyway, so the practical loss is small.

The names, the tooltip and the multiplicity glyph need one field each published to the designs first.

Between the two designs at the same screen

  • The tab strip is at the bottom in design 1 and the top in design 2, with different cell widths in all three looks.
  • Grabbable handles exist in design 1 (y-gauge, ladder counter) and in neither screen of design 2, though your ruling was for both. OPEN WORK
  • Design 1 names the sort key in its hint row on every screen; design 2 names it nowhere.
  • Label clicks: design 1's prism number tags pick, its ladder letter tags clear; design 2's star names and roman numerals both pick.
  • Design 1 shows a list on every screen; design 2 only at PRISM, behind L.
  • In design 1 the tab band and the commit bar share one row of texels at the bottom; the tab wins, at the one screen where the commit click is live.
  • V is printed nowhere in any look.

What to change

Two groups. The first are defects with no design question in them; one "go" covers the lot. The second are things the old nav had that the new one does not, and each needs your yes, no, or park. Answer by number.

A · Defects — say "go" and I fix them, no ruling needed

  1. The commit row (design 1) and the WARP chip (design 2) are drawn armed on every screen but only answer a click at SYSTEM. Enter works everywhere; the button lies on four screens. Recommend: the click does what Enter does.
  2. The selection never clears: with nothing picked, both designs frame a fallback body and say BURN TO it; picking the star leaves the frame on a planet. You cannot tell armed from unarmed. Recommend: a real no-selection state, and a star selection that the frame follows.
  3. The 2D maps outrun the pointer when dragged: 1.35× in design 1, 1.4× and 2.6× in design 2. One scale constant from the old 160-px map is applied to three different drawn sizes. Recommend: scale by the drawn map.
  4. A drag that starts on the rail, the tabs, the status line or the commit row still pans or rotates the map. Recommend: only a press on the map starts a gesture.
  5. Keys act on screens where nothing shows it: , . on every design-1 screen; L, [ ], - = on four of five design-2 screens; and L on a 2D screen arms invisible list rows that steal map clicks. Recommend: each key bound only where it draws something.
  6. After one V cycle the old nav opens its prism and orrery at the designs' angles, not its own. Measured live. The "old nav unchanged" guarantee only holds until you press V. Recommend: restore the old defaults on the way back.
  7. Right-click "go back" is dead in every look. Recommend: bind it properly, since the designs otherwise have Shift+Tab and legacy has only the tabs.
  8. Under the designs the × close button is off-screen and the backdrop cannot be clicked. Recommend: fix the CSS.
  9. HERE · SECTOR at SYSTEM clears the body selection instead of doing nothing. Recommend: eat the click until you rule what it should do there.
  10. Multiple-star pips never draw and the COMPS sort does nothing, because the field they read is never filled. Recommend: fill it.
  11. Design 1's tab band and commit bar overlap by one texel; at SYSTEM the tab wins the commit's top row. Recommend: move the bar down one texel.
  12. Hidden controls with no legend: V everywhere; / on design 1's PRISM and SYSTEM; RF on design 1's PRISM; the sort key and page keys in design 2; any legend at all on design 2's SYSTEM; Shift+Tab. Recommend: print them.

B · Restorations — each needs your yes, no, or park

  1. Hover-inspect on every screen: sector name at GALAXY, coordinates at SECTOR and REGION, the star tooltip at PRISM, the body callout at SYSTEM. Loss #1. It is the only way to learn what a thing is without selecting it. Recommend: yes, PRISM and SYSTEM first.
  2. The prism's depth cues: drop lines to the plane, the plane grid, far-first drawing; plus spectral colour and the catalogue halo in design 1. This is the "too simplistic" table above; the lines are cheap because both ends are already computed. Recommend: yes, keep the low-fi marks.
  3. Names on the prism in design 1 (in place of, or beside, the eight digits) and the height numbers in both: HEIGHT with its region, PLAYER Y, Y RANGE. Recommend: names yes; numbers into design 1's detail block and design 2's status line.
  4. Planet detail with moons, and moons as burn targets. Loss #2. Needs a design-side sub-view, not a switch back to the old one. Recommend: yes.
  5. The ship's real position at SYSTEM, and the trajectory line to the selected body. Recommend: yes.
  6. Wheel zoom at SYSTEM. Recommend: design 2 yes; design 1 no, its ladder is a scroll, not a zoom.
  7. Body names on the ladder and the orrery, placed like the prism labels, in place of or beside the letter and roman tags. Recommend: yes.
  8. Belt names, a line of facts about the star, and the wide-binary member list with its sub-view. Recommend: belts and the star line yes; binaries park.
  9. One zoom readout for all three looks, same quantity and unit. Today: radius in ly (old), nothing (design 1), diameter in pc (design 2). Recommend: yes, pick one.
  10. The AUTOPILOT toggle under the designs. Recommend: park; it is inert in ORRERY anyway.
  11. Grabbable handles in design 2 to match design 1. Your ruling was look-agnostic; only design 1 has them. Recommend: yes, already open work.
